items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I said, 'Hey Eric, this is what Travis played.' ... he did a voice of a chord so I still use that voicing that he showed me, all the time.

ctx.x: Man you’ve had quite a career. And it’s active now in the education part of it at William Paterson, it added a lot for you?

Right. Yeah, it’s been, because this sounds like a redundant statement but as Ted Dunbar used to say teaching is learning and learning is teaching and it’s true. Because if you get students, especially if you’ve got students who can already play, and you show them something, then they say, “You mean do it like this?” And you say, “Wait a minute, what was that?” Yeah okay. I’ll keep it for myself. So I teach but I also learn. Like I was saying earlier, I played this song, and I said, “Hey Eric, this is what Travis…
Let me run a couple of names by you and just get your impression of these musicians. One is Cannonball Adderley.
